extraction.name: MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark
extraction.description: The Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) spans 8 embedding tasks covering a total of 58 datasets and 112 languages to provide a comprehensive benchmark of text embeddings.
extraction.creator: Niklas Muennighoff, Nouamane Tazi, Loïc Magne, Nils Reimers
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MTEB unifies datasets from different embedding tasks into a common evaluation framework. It incorporates existing datasets like SemEval and BEIR, and includes custom-made datasets created using public APIs from arXiv and bioRxiv/medRxiv, as well as available data from Reddit and StackExchange posts.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Existing NLP benchmark datasets, public APIs from arXiv and bioRxiv/medRxiv, and available data from Reddit and StackExchange posts.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For custom clustering datasets, S2S datasets use the title of the paper as input text, while P2P datasets use the concatenation of the title and the abstract. Cluster labels are generated using human-assigned categories, with splits created based on main and secondary categories.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: MTEB imposes no limit on the input length, leaving it up to the models to truncate if necessary.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For custom clustering datasets, cluster labels are generated using categories given to the papers by humans.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: MTEB is versioned at a dataset and software level. The benchmark welcomes dataset, task, or metric contributions from the community via pull requests to continue its development.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limitations include the absence of very long document datasets, task imbalance (average scores are biased towards tasks with many datasets), lack of multilingual datasets for retrieval and clustering, absence of code datasets, and lack of benchmarking for additional modalities.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating and benchmarking text embedding models across 8 tasks: Bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, Semantic Textual Similarity (STS), and summarization.
